prompts.takabe: Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent PNG sprite atlas for Japanese fishing game. Match the natural anatomical pixel-painted, detailed retro fish illustration style of the references already shown, but absolutely no glow or background. Exactly eight isolated whole fish of one species, no labels or extra objects, each fully inside its own spacious cell. Landscape 1536x1024 atlas, four columns by two rows. Row one left-to-right: full profile facing RIGHT (tail left, mouth right); three-quarter facing RIGHT; almost frontal angled slightly RIGHT; symmetrical straight frontal. Row two left-to-right: almost frontal angled slightly LEFT; three-quarter facing LEFT; full profile facing LEFT (mouth left, tail right); full profile facing RIGHT with open biting mouth. Each view must depict the same species. Maintain the 8 poses precisely. Natural fish anatomy, fins and complete tail and all appendages, no clipping or overlap, clean outlined silhouettes and real transparent alpha. No background, shadow, aura, border, text or water. Species: Takabe, Labracoglossa argentiventris. Streamlined small fusiform fish, blue to blue-gray dorsal region, silver white belly, a very clear vivid yellow horizontal stripe from just BEHIND the eye along the upper flank all the way into a deeply forked yellow caudal tail. Relatively small mouth, small scales, continuous spiny dorsal fin; yellowish lower fins. No black shoulder spot (not a striped jack), no oversized jack-like body. Bright distinctive yellow stripe and tail.

measurementMethod: Eight-connectivity components at alpha >= 48, matching fish-art.js isolation threshold. Bounding boxes use x,y,width,height in atlas pixels. Mouth anchors are manually inspected lip centers, normalized within each box. Original generated RGBA files copied without raster edits.
validation: All three 1536x1024 atlases contain eight separate whole fish in requested pose order. Species-defining yellow stripe/forked tail, dark operculum edge, and paired chin barbels/caudal saddle are present.
